lines.text: David, in the Wilderness of Judah, says his soul thirsts for God in a dry and weary land.
David has seen God's power and glory in the sanctuary, and says God's loving devotion is better than life.
David will bless God as long as he lives, lifting his hands in God's name, and remembers Him on his bed.
David says God is his help, so he sings for joy in the shadow of God's tower, and God's right hand upholds him.
Those who seek David's life will fall to the sword and become a portion for foxes, but the priest will rejoice in God.
